projects.title: My Personal Bookshelf (That Everyone Can Use)
projects.summary:
I was really inspired by Beli's (a restaurant list-keeping app) relative ranking system, and this app adapts the same comparison-based approach to books. A custom ranking wizard places each book within a user's existing library through direct comparisons, which works to enable more precise and consistent rankings over time.

Beyond just ranking, this platform functions as a daily reading companion, allowing users to import libraries from Goodreads, add new books, and fully customize their bookshelf through themes, colors, fonts, and layout. This project was built as a highly personal reading platform that combines structured ranking with deep visual customization.
projects.description:
The Personal Library Management System is an interactive web application for building and exploring a personal reading library. Users can add books via the Open Library API, import full collections from Goodreads CSV exports, and organize titles across dynamic shelves for books they want to read, are currently reading, or have finished.

A core feature is the ranking wizard, which places completed books into a precise ranked order using pairwise comparisons. The system applies a binary search strategy to minimize comparisons while enforcing rating constraints, ensuring higher-rated books never fall below lower-rated ones. Rankings can also be adjusted manually via drag-and-drop, with derived ratings computed on a normalized 0–10 scale.

The application's centerpiece is a real-time bookshelf renderer built on the Canvas API. It generates photorealistic book spines by extracting dominant colors from cover art, calculating physical dimensions, and dynamically fitting rotated spine text. Users can fully customize the visual style through a theme manager that supports preset palettes, custom color selection, bulk styling, and live font previews. Shelves support progressive rendering animations, hover interactions, and exportable image downloads.

Beyond visualization, the system supports reading goals with real-time progress tracking, custom color-coded tags, advanced filtering, and detailed statistics. Books can be linked through "thought continuations," forming a directed graph that maps conceptual connections between readings. Public profile pages allow users to share their libraries and view others' collections and progress.

The platform is built with a React and TypeScript frontend and a Flask backend, supporting seamless migration from SQLite in development to PostgreSQL in production on Heroku. The architecture includes session-based authentication, REST APIs, caching strategies, and high-performance canvas rendering for large collections.
